**Answer: In the combined logistic regression model including BMI, age, and gender as predictors of treatment response (partial response, PR), the p-value for age is p = 0.0025 (Age coefficient −0.0795, SE 0.0263, z = −3.02; OR = 0.924, 95% CI 0.877–0.972). Age is a statistically significant predictor — each additional year of age is associated with ~7.6% lower odds of PR, adjusting for BMI and gender.**

Full model details (n = 80; PR = 41, non-PR [PD+SD] = 39; converged in 5 iterations, McFadden pseudo-R² = 0.124, no separation):

| Predictor | Coef | SE | z | p | OR | 95% CI |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Intercept | 0.9181 | 2.7887 | 0.33 | 0.742 | 2.50 | (0.011, 592.2) |
| BMI | 0.1621 | 0.1088 | 1.49 | 0.136 | 1.176 | (0.950, 1.456) |
| **Age** | **−0.0795** | **0.0263** | **−3.02** | **0.0025** | **0.924** | **(0.877, 0.972)** |
| Gender (Female vs Male) | 0.6132 | 0.5471 | 1.12 | 0.262 | 1.846 | (0.632, 5.395) |

Coding notes: PR was coded 1 with PD and SD pooled as 0; Age and BMI entered as continuous predictors; Gender as a binary indicator (Female=1 vs Male reference) — as stated earlier, the choice of gender reference level does not affect the Age p-value.
